HubspotCalendarService awaits this and types it as HubspotToken, then computes expiry from `expiresIn` — accessing `.expires_in` on a Response object yields undefined, producing NaN stored in the credential key. The diff shows the type mismatch directly.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw `fetch` Response when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts). Hubspot’s CalendarService now does `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` (packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts) and then proceeds as if it received a parsed token object. Unlike other integrations (e.g., O365/Zoom) that parse the response body after `refreshOAuthTokens`, Hubspot does not, so in sync mode it will be operating on a Response object, making token fields (like expiry-related values) undefined and leading to incorrect expiry computation/storage.
